content.title: Mercedes reports plunge in Q3 operating profit, hit by job cuts
content.summary:
STORY: Mercedes-Benz reported stronger than expected margins at its core autos business Wednesday (October 29).

The German auto giant saw improved sales of premium models.

That helped offset falling sales in China and one-off charges related to ongoing job cuts.

Mercedes faces particular challenges in the Chinese premium and luxury market, like its rivals Porsche and BMW.

Local carmakers have driven a price war which has hit demand.

CEO Ola Kaellenius said the carmaker didn't want to join the price war despite the difficulties it faces in China.

U.S. import tariffs have also weighed on auto companies.

Mercedes-Benz's return on sales at its car division was 4.8% in the third quarter, up from last year and well ahead of analyst expectations.

This was helped by a 10% increase in top-end models, while free cash flow was about $1.6 billion.

It led the automaker to resume its share buyback program.

However, operating profit fell 70% owing to charges related to layoffs.

The company is implementing restructuring measures to save around $5.8 billion globally by 2027.

Shares in the company were up 6% in early trade to hit a seven-month high.

Mercedes' challenges are spread across its most important markets.

It faces tariffs in the U.S., and a highly competitive Chinese market.

While European emissions targets have led to a challenging shift towards electric vehicles.

content.title: Engaged Capital urges cost cutting at Cognex to boost share price
content.summary: NEW YORK (Reuters) -Activist investor Engaged Capital has built a sizable stake in Cognex and is urging the maker of machine vision systems to cut costs and use cost consultants, arguing this could help the stock price nearly double in the next two years.  "This is an AI company without the AI valuation," Engaged's founder and chief investment officer Glenn Welling said on Tuesday at the 13D Monitor Active-Passive Investment Summit in New York.
